title: The two-coordinate Witt extension and its canonical Verschiebung
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] of prime characteristic $p>0$. Let $c_p(X,Y)\in k[X,Y]$ be the reduction of the integral polynomial $-\sum_{i=1}^{p-1}(\binom pi/p)X^iY^{p-i}$. The affine plane $W_{2,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[X_0,X_1]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] is a commutative affine finite-type $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] for the law on every commutative $k$-algebra $R$ given by $(a,b)+(a',b')=(a+a',b+b'+c_p(a,a'))$, with zero $(0,0)$. The homomorphisms $j:\mathbf G_a\to W_{2,k}$, $t\mapsto(0,t)$, and $\tau:W_{2,k}\to\mathbf G_a$, $(a,b)\mapsto a$, form an exact sequence $0\to\mathbf G_a\xrightarrow{j}W_{2,k}\xrightarrow{\tau}\mathbf G_a\to0$: $j$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] identifying its source with the scheme-theoretic kernel, and $\tau$ is faithfully flat (flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]) and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The group $\mathbf G_a$ is [def-sc-gm-ga]. Under the canonical identification $W_{2,k}^{(p)}\simeq W_{2,k}$ from these formulas over $\mathbf F_p$, the canonical Verschiebung of [lem-sfb-affine-group-frobenius-verschiebung] is $(a,b)\mapsto(0,a)$; likewise $V_{\mathbf G_a}=0$. The subscript 2 here denotes two coordinates, independently of alternative indexing conventions for Witt schemes.

source.place: Section 11(j), printed pp.226-227: addition polynomial S_1, Proposition 11.44 and the paragraph following it computing Verschiebung as shift then truncation. This uses the two-coordinate group called W_2 in Proposition 15.27, printed p.316; it is W_1 in the zero-based formulas of Section 11(j).

proof.text:
Work first in integral polynomial rings. For $1\leq i<p$, $p\mid\binom pi$: in $p!=\binom pi i!(p-i)!$ the latter two factorials are prime to $p$. Thus $C(X,Y)=-\sum_{i=1}^{p-1}(\binom pi/p)X^iY^{p-i}$ is integral and satisfies $pC(X,Y)=X^p+Y^p-(X+Y)^p$. Symmetry and $C(X,0)=0$ follow termwise. Expanding the last identity gives
$$p\bigl(C(X,Y)+C(X+Y,Z)-C(Y,Z)-C(X,Y+Z)\bigr)=0.$$
Multiplication by $p$ is injective coefficientwise over $\mathbf Z$, so the parenthesized polynomial is zero. Reduction to $k$ gives the same identities for $c_p$. All evaluations used below are the universal polynomial evaluations, so these are identities over every commutative $k$-algebra, including ones with nilpotents.

source.place: 11(j), p.226, displayed polynomial S_1; its integral cocycle identity expanded explicitly

proof.text: Put $A=k[X_0,X_1]$ and identify $A\otimes_kA$ with $k[X_0,X_1,Y_0,Y_1]$, $X_i\otimes1\mapsto X_i$, $1\otimes X_i\mapsto Y_i$, by the tensor pushout property and the polynomial universal property (mutually inverse on generators). Define $k$-algebra maps on generators: $\Delta(X_0)=X_0+Y_0$, $\Delta(X_1)=X_1+Y_1+c_p(X_0,Y_0)$; $\epsilon(X_i)=0$; $S(X_0)=-X_0$, $S(X_1)=-X_1-c_p(X_0,-X_0)$. Each Hopf identity of [lem-sfb-hopf-spectrum-functor] is an equality of algebra maps out of $A$, so it suffices to check it on $X_0,X_1$. On $X_1$, coassociativity compares $c_p(a,a')+c_p(a+a',a'')$ with $c_p(a',a'')+c_p(a,a'+a'')$, equal by step 1; the counit identities use $c_p(X,0)=c_p(0,Y)=0$; the antipode identities give $-c_p(X_0,-X_0)+c_p(-X_0,X_0)=0$ and its mirror by symmetry; on $X_0$ all are additive. Symmetry also gives $\mathrm{swap}\circ\Delta=\Delta$. Hence [lem-sfb-hopf-spectrum-functor] makes $W_{2,k}=\operatorname{Spec}A$ an affine $k$-group scheme, commutative since $m\circ s$ has comorphism $\mathrm{swap}\circ\Delta$. On $R$-points $x,y:A\to R$ the sum is $(x\otimes y)\Delta$, which is the displayed law. Finite type: the one affine chart has algebra generated by $X_0,X_1$ over $k$ and is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs].

source.place: 11.43, pp.226-227, polynomial group operations; two-coordinate verification

proof.text: The comorphisms $j^*:A\to k[t]$, $X_0\mapsto0$, $X_1\mapsto t$, and $\tau^*:k[t]\to A$, $t\mapsto X_0$, preserve comultiplication, counit and antipode on generators: for $j^*$ this uses $c_p(0,0)=0$, for $\tau^*$ the first-coordinate formula. So $j$ and $\tau$ are homomorphisms by [lem-sfb-hopf-spectrum-functor]. $j^*$ is surjective with kernel $(X_0)$, so the affine closed-immersion criterion, applied to the one-member affine cover of $W_{2,k}$, makes $j$ a closed immersion. The scheme-theoretic kernel of $\tau$ is $W_{2,k}\times_{\mathbf G_a,\tau,e}\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $e^*(t)=0$; by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] it is $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{k[t]}k)$, and $A\otimes_{k[t]}k=A/(X_0)\cong k[X_1]$: the tensor pushout property says precisely that an algebra map out of this ring is a map out of $A$ killing $X_0$. Under this isomorphism the kernel inclusion is $j$, and its law is ordinary addition on $X_1$, as required for $\mathbf G_a$.

source.place: 11.44, p.227, kernel of truncation; explicit closed-immersion and fibre-ring checks

proof.text: The comorphism of $\tau$ identifies $A$ with $B[X_1]$ over $B=k[X_0]$. Hence $\tau$ is flat by [lem-nagata-polynomial-projection-flat]. Its scheme section $s(a)=(a,0)$ satisfies $\tau s=1$, proving surjectivity on points; no assertion that $s$ preserves the group law is needed. It is locally of finite presentation: use the global affine source and target charts and the presentation $B[X_1]$ with one generator and no relations. For the remaining finite-presentation conditions, $\tau$ is affine by [pqf-lem-affine-local-target], using the one-member affine cover $\{\operatorname{Spec}B\}$ of the target, whose preimage $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine. The affine-morphism permanence theorem gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Thus $\tau$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented, which with step 3 is the stated exact sequence.

source.place: 11.44, p.227; flatness and finite presentation of coordinate projection made explicit

proof.text:
For the same law over $\mathbf Z$, the $n$-fold sum of $(a,b)$, for each integer $n\geq1$, is
$$\left(na,nb+\frac{n-n^p}{p}a^p\right).$$
Here $n-n^p$ is divisible by $p$: induct from $0$ using $(n+1)^p\equiv n^p+1\pmod p$ and the binomial divisibilities in step 1. The formula starts at $n=1$. For its induction step, the additional correction is $C(na,a)=\bigl(n^p+1-(n+1)^p\bigr)a^p/p$; adding it changes $(n-n^p)/p$ to $((n+1)-(n+1)^p)/p$, exactly as asserted. Set $n=p$ and reduce to characteristic $p$. Since $p\geq2$, $1-p^{p-1}$ reduces to $1$, and therefore $[p]_{W_2}(a,b)=(0,a^p)$. This calculation is an integral polynomial calculation before reduction, not division by $p$ inside $k$.

source.place: 11(j), p.227, direct verification of VF=p, specialized to the two-coordinate addition polynomial

proof.text:
All addition and inverse polynomials have coefficients in $\mathbf F_p$. The twist identification on coordinates is the $k$-algebra isomorphism
$$A^{(p)}=A\otimes_{k,\sigma}k\longrightarrow k[U_0,U_1],\quad f\otimes c\longmapsto c f^{[p]}(U_0,U_1),$$
where $\sigma(r)=r^p$ and $f^{[p]}$ raises coefficients, not exponents, to their $p$-th powers. It respects $(rf)\otimes c=f\otimes r^pc$; its inverse fixes $k$ and sends $U_i$ to $X_i\otimes1$. These formulas are mutually inverse on coefficients and monomials. The structure polynomials are unchanged under coefficient Frobenius, so this is an identification of group schemes. Under it the relative Frobenius comorphism in [lem-sfb-affine-group-frobenius-verschiebung] is the $k$-linear map $f^*:k[U_0,U_1]\to A$, $U_i\mapsto X_i^p$. It is injective, since distinct monomials $U_0^rU_1^s$ have distinct images $X_0^{pr}X_1^{ps}$ in the monomial basis. No inverse of $\sigma:k\to k$ is used.

source.place: 11(j), p.227, canonical twist identification and coordinate Frobenius; tensor relation and injectivity written out

proof.text: Let $U:W_2^{(p)}\to W_2$ be the polynomial morphism $(a,b)\mapsto(0,a)$ under step 6. It is a homomorphism, since the first coordinate of addition is additive and $c_p(0,0)=0$. Steps 5-6 give $UF_{W_2}=[p]_{W_2}$. The canonical map $V$ from [lem-sfb-affine-group-frobenius-verschiebung] satisfies the same identity $VF_{W_2}=[p]_{W_2}$. On coordinate rings this reads $f^*U^*=f^*V^*$. Injectivity of $f^*$ from step 6 implies $U^*=V^*$; the spectrum correspondence gives $U=V$, proving the canonical, rather than merely an additive, shift formula. For $\mathbf G_a$, its additive law gives $[p]=0$. Its relative Frobenius comorphism is $k[U]\to k[X]$, $U\mapsto X^p$, again injective by the monomial basis. The identity $V_{\mathbf G_a}F_{\mathbf G_a}=0$ therefore gives $V_{\mathbf G_a}^*(X)=0$, which is exactly the zero group homomorphism. This also covers $p=2$.

source.place: 11(j), p.227, Verschiebung is shift then truncation and V_Ga=0; identification using 11.40(a)
